headline: AI's Honesty Gap
thesis: Students say their peers misuse AI far more than they do, while Title I schools risk falling behind and Google's AI-search deadline nears.
summary: A new NBER survey covered by Inside Higher Ed finds only 23% of college students admit using AI to draft essays, while 54% say their peers do, adding to this week's debate about AI suspicion on campus. In K-12, EdSurge asks what happens when AI outruns Title I schools, and Google faces a Nov. 30 deadline to answer Sen. Markey about its plan to tie school Search access to its AI features. On procurement, district leaders continue to say trust and evidence matter more than features. Campus governance news includes Mott Community College removing its president, NYC's new university tech-transfer deals and a temporary dismissal of the government's Harvard admissions-data case. Standards work closes out the year with the QTI survey due Nov. 30, a CLR 2.0 showcase on Dec. 3 and Blackboard's Dec. 31 LTI 1.3 deadline.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · NOVEMBER 25, 2026 · Thanksgiving week: several sources had no new posts, so recent items are shown. Research used web search because direct page fetches were blocked in this run; dates come from search listings.
